SHW.rationale: SHW is a high-quality franchise with dominant market share (~69% U.S. Paint Stores), demonstrated pricing power (7% price increase effective Jan 2026), and stable gross margins at ~49%. Q1 2026 showed healthy YoY growth: revenue +6.8%, EPS +7.5%, with revenue beating consensus. The stock has de-rated meaningfully — P/E compressed from ~33x to ~30.6x (near 1-year trough of 29.4x), P/B from 21.6x to 17.9x — while fundamentals remain intact. This creates a mild quality-at-a-discount setup. However, conviction is tempered by: (1) poor Q1 OCF/NI conversion of 0.26x with incomplete trailing cash-flow data; (2) leverage of 2.5x net debt/EBITDA on $11.7B total debt in a rising-rate environment (10Y at 4.41% vs 3.3% earnings yield — no equity risk premium); (3) macro headwinds from oil at $98.38/bbl pressuring raw material costs; and (4) CEO's own caution of 'little to no recovery' in end markets. The BPA regulatory ban in Q2 2026 provides a modest, dated catalyst for packaging coatings, and Q2/Q3 seasonal cash generation should normalize, but these are incremental rather than transformative. Score sits between the the25 — above neutral on franchise durability and valuation discount, but below +0.3 given leverage, macro uncertainty.
